guide.name: MLB ballparks from Fenway to Dodger Stadium
guide.description: All 30 major league ballparks as of 2026, from Fenway and Wrigley to the Athletics' temporary home in West Sacramento, with a classic local place to eat or drink near about half of them.

properties.name: Fenway Park
properties.notes: The oldest park in the majors, open since 1912. Look for the single red seat high in the right-field bleachers that marks Ted Williams's longest home run, and Pesky's Pole down the short right-field line.

properties.name: Cask'n Flagon
properties.notes: The sports bar across Brookline Avenue from the back of the Green Monster, pouring since 1969. Gets loud before first pitch and stays that way after the last out.

properties.name: Yankee Stadium
properties.notes: Get in early for Monument Park behind the center-field fence, with plaques and retired numbers going back to Babe Ruth. It closes before first pitch; check the team site for the cutoff.

properties.name: Yankee Tavern
properties.notes: An old-school tavern a block from the stadium, around since the 1920s, with Yankees history on every wall and a pub menu that holds up before or after a game.

properties.name: Citi Field
properties.notes: Enter through the Jackie Robinson Rotunda, modeled on Ebbets Field. The old Home Run Apple from Shea Stadium sits outside the gate, and a newer one rises in center field after Mets homers.

properties.name: Citizens Bank Park
properties.notes: Walk Ashburn Alley behind the outfield for cheesesteaks and the Phillies' Wall of Fame. The giant neon Liberty Bell in right-center rings and lights up after Phillies home runs.

properties.name: PNC Park
properties.notes: Arguably the best view in baseball: downtown Pittsburgh framed over the outfield across the Allegheny. The classic approach is on foot from downtown over the yellow Roberto Clemente Bridge.

properties.name: Primanti Bros.
properties.notes: The original Strip District counter, where the fries and coleslaw go inside the sandwich. About two miles up the river from PNC Park; expect a line on game days.

properties.name: Oriole Park at Camden Yards
properties.notes: The 1992 park that set the template for the retro ballparks that followed. Eutaw Street runs between the stands and the long brick B&O Warehouse, with brass plaques where home runs landed and Boog's BBQ smoking away.

properties.name: Pickles Pub
properties.notes: A sports bar across Washington Boulevard from the ballpark, with a back patio and a crowd in orange before every home game. The default pregame stop for Orioles fans.

properties.name: Nationals Park
properties.notes: Stay in your seat for the fourth-inning Presidents Race, with giant-headed Washington, Jefferson, Lincoln and Teddy Roosevelt sprinting down the warning track. The Anacostia riverfront is a short walk away.
properties.address: 1500 S Capitol St SE, Washington, DC 20003

properties.name: Ben's Chili Bowl
properties.notes: A U Street landmark since 1958 that kept serving through decades of change in the neighborhood. Order the chili half-smoke. It's about three miles north of the ballpark, a straight shot on the Green Line.

properties.name: Rogers Centre
properties.notes: The first ballpark with a fully retractable roof, under the CN Tower. A hotel has rooms that look straight onto the field, and the renovated outfield now has open-air social decks. Bring a passport.
properties.address: 1 Blue Jays Way, Toronto, ON M5V 1J1, Canada

properties.name: Truist Park
properties.notes: Out in Cobb County, about ten miles northwest of downtown, inside the Battery's restaurants and bars. The street number is a nod to Hank Aaron's 755 home runs; his statue stands in the Monument Garden on the concourse.

properties.name: loanDepot park
properties.notes: A retractable-roof park on the old Orange Bowl site. The colorful home run sculpture that once sat in center field now stands out on the plaza, which is the best place for photos.

properties.name: Versailles Restaurant
properties.notes: Miami's best-known Cuban restaurant, on Calle Ocho since 1971. Order a cafecito and a pastry at the walk-up window if you don't want a full meal of ropa vieja. About two miles from the ballpark.

properties.name: Tropicana Field
properties.notes: The Rays came home in 2026 after Hurricane Milton tore off the roof in 2024. It's the only fixed dome in the majors, with catwalks that have their own ground rules. Check team news on plans for a new ballpark.

properties.name: Wrigley Field
properties.notes: Open since 1914, with ivy on the outfield brick and a center-field scoreboard still changed by hand. Look across Waveland and Sheffield for the rooftop bleachers on the apartment buildings.

properties.name: Murphy's Bleachers
properties.notes: The corner bar at Sheffield and Waveland, steps from the bleacher gate. A Wrigleyville fixture that fills up hours before first pitch and empties straight into the bleachers.

properties.name: Rate Field
properties.notes: The White Sox park on the South Side, with an exploding scoreboard whose pinwheels spin after home runs, carried over from old Comiskey Park. Comiskey's home plate is marked in the parking lot to the north.

properties.name: American Family Field
properties.notes: Arrive early: tailgating in the parking lots is part of the ritual here. Inside, watch for Bernie Brewer's slide after Brewers home runs and the sausage race in the sixth inning under the fan-shaped retractable roof.

properties.name: Target Field
properties.notes: Built with Minnesota limestone and squeezed into the North Loop, with light rail stopping at the gate. The Minnie and Paul sign in center field lights up when the Twins homer.

properties.name: Comerica Park
properties.notes: Big stone tigers guard the gates, and inside there's a carousel and a Ferris wheel with baseball-shaped cars. After the Fifth Third and Comerica bank merger, expect a new name; check the Tigers site for the current one.

properties.name: American Coney Island
properties.notes: The Detroit coney dog, with chili, mustard and onions, served since 1917 right next door to its rival, Lafayette Coney Island. About a mile south of the ballpark.

properties.name: Progressive Field
properties.notes: Opened as Jacobs Field in 1994 and recently renovated. Heritage Park, behind the center-field wall, honors the Guardians' greats, and the downtown skyline rises over left field.

properties.name: Great Lakes Brewing Co.
properties.notes: A brewpub since 1988 in old brick buildings next to the West Side Market, across the river from the ballpark. Order the Edmund Fitzgerald porter.

properties.name: Great American Ball Park
properties.notes: Twin riverboat smokestacks beyond right-center shoot fireworks after Reds home runs. The Reds Hall of Fame and Museum is next to the main gate, and the Ohio River runs past the outfield.

properties.name: Arnold's Bar and Grill
properties.notes: Cincinnati's oldest tavern, open since 1861, with a covered courtyard out back. About a mile north of the ballpark.

properties.name: Busch Stadium
properties.notes: Upper-deck seats behind home plate frame the Gateway Arch over the outfield. Ballpark Village across Clark Avenue holds the Cardinals Hall of Fame and Museum.

properties.name: Kauffman Stadium
properties.notes: The fountains and waterfalls beyond the outfield wall are the largest privately funded fountain display in the world. Grab a seat out in the outfield to get misted on a hot night.

properties.name: Globe Life Field
properties.notes: An air-conditioned park with a retractable roof, built so Texas summers don't wreck the game. It sits between the Rangers' old park and the Cowboys' stadium, with the Texas Live! district across the street.

properties.name: Daikin Park
properties.notes: The Astros' park, called Minute Maid Park until 2025, built into the old Union Station. A replica locomotive rolls along the left-field wall after Astros home runs, above the short porch of the Crawford Boxes.

properties.name: The Original Ninfa's on Navigation
properties.notes: The East End Tex-Mex restaurant Mama Ninfa Laurenzo opened in 1973, credited with putting fajitas on the map in Houston. About a mile east of the ballpark.

properties.name: Chase Field
properties.notes: There's a swimming pool beyond the right-center field wall, rented as a suite. The infield keeps an old-fashioned dirt path from the mound to home plate, and the roof closes for summer heat.

properties.name: Coors Field
properties.notes: A row of purple seats in the upper deck marks exactly one mile above sea level. Balls fly in the thin air, which is why the Rockies keep game balls in a humidor.

properties.name: Wynkoop Brewing Company
properties.notes: Colorado's first brewpub, opened in 1988 in an old LoDo warehouse two blocks from Coors Field. Pool tables upstairs and plenty of room for a postgame crowd.

properties.name: Dodger Stadium
properties.notes: Open since 1962 in Chavez Ravine, with palm trees and the San Gabriel Mountains beyond the outfield at sunset. Have a Dodger Dog, and stay for the view from the top deck as the sun goes down.
properties.address: 1000 Vin Scully Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90012

properties.name: Philippe the Original
properties.notes: A 1908 deli near Union Station that claims to have invented the French dip. Order it double-dipped with a dab of the hot mustard. About a mile and a half from Dodger Stadium.
properties.address: 1001 N Alameda St, Los Angeles, CA 90012

properties.name: Angel Stadium
properties.notes: The giant Big A sign in the parking lot lights its halo after Angels wins. Beyond center field, a fake rock formation with waterfalls and geysers goes off after home runs.
properties.address: 2000 E Gene Autry Way, Anaheim, CA 92806

properties.name: Petco Park
properties.notes: The old Western Metal Supply Co. building is built into the left-field corner, with seats on its roof. Gallagher Square, the grassy area beyond the outfield, is a low-cost way to watch a game from the lawn.

properties.name: Oracle Park
properties.notes: Home runs over the right-field wall land in McCovey Cove, where kayakers wait for splash hits. Get the garlic fries and bring a jacket; night games turn cold off the bay.

properties.name: Sutter Health Park
properties.notes: The Athletics' temporary home through 2027, before their planned move to Las Vegas, shared with the Triple-A River Cats. The smallest park in the majors, with a lawn berm in the outfield and the gold Tower Bridge a short walk away.

properties.name: T-Mobile Park
properties.notes: The retractable roof works like an umbrella: it covers the field when it rains but leaves the sides open. The upper concourse looks out over downtown and Elliott Bay.
